stanzas: Bogv rodzicza dzewicza bogem slawena maria
Vtwego syna gospodzina matko swolena maria
orig.credit: Anonymous; the two oldest stanzas, in the spelling of the earliest manuscript

stanzas: Mother of God, virgin, by God glorified, Mary,
From your son the Lord, chosen mother, Mary,
Win for us, send down to us. Kyrie eleison.
For your Baptist's sake, O Son of God,
Hear the voices, fulfil the thoughts of man,
Hear the prayer that we bring,
And deign to give what we ask:
and in the world a godly dwelling,
after life a stay in paradise. Kyrie eleison.

notes: IMPORT: the '¦' in line 2.3 ('modlitwo¦ yo¦sz') stands for the manuscript's nasal-vowel letter, lost in the import (read 'modlitwę, jąż'). Line 2.6 'pzbith' is missing the manuscript's abbreviation mark (read 'przebyt'), and 'ky’eleyson' has an apostrophe for an abbreviation sign. Check orig against the manuscript image or a diplomatic edition before publishing.
line 1.1: 'bogiem sławiena' is read as 'glorified by God'; some read it as 'famed for (bearing) God' [?].
line 1.2: 'U twego syna Gospodzina': 'from' (or 'with, at') your son the Lord; the petition is that Mary win from him what follows.
line 1.3: 'Zyszczy nam, spuści nam': obtain (win) for us, send down to us; the object (forgiveness, grace) is not said.
line 2.1: 'Twego dziela Krzciciela, Bożycze': 'Bożyc' is the Son of God (vocative); 'your Baptist' is John the Baptist, invoked as intercessor (the Deesis).
line 2.2: 'napełń myśli', literally 'fill (fulfil) the thoughts', i.e. grant what people intend.
line 2.5: 'zbożny pobyt' is disputed: a pious life, or a prosperous one ('zboże' once meant wealth, fortune). Rendered 'godly dwelling' [?].
line 2.6: 'przebyt' (a dwelling, a stay) after life; rendered 'a stay in paradise'.
Kyrie eleison (Greek, 'Lord, have mercy') kept as it stands.
